brief: Nvidia's co-founder and only CEO in 33 years, Jensen Huang, resigned effective immediately amid a spy-affair scandal and FBI investigation, and 14 sellside desks cut ratings or price targets overnight. The stock gapped down about 12% to near $159 before clawing back half the drop. Retail met the open with $111 million of net buying in 30 minutes, 41 times normal and Vanda Research's largest opening bid ever recorded in NVDA, more than double its 99th-percentile reading. Vanda's historical pattern points to $450-770 million of buying by the close, and the three-day total through Wednesday reached $1.31 billion, 61% of all US retail buying this week, with leveraged 2x NVDA ETFs also seeing near-record inflows while inverse funds saw none. Yet the stock is still down 15% in five days, and $1.3 billion is only 0.03% of Nvidia's market cap. Zero Hedge argues institutions are using the retail bid as exit liquidity rather than a bottom signal, noting record retail buying has rarely marked the low, with a DOJ antitrust probe, Huang's possible testimony, an open CEO search, and earnings next Tuesday still ahead.
